title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the streets and corridors surrounding Bowdoin College, from the historic Federal Street district to the bustling shops of Maine Street.

cards.title: The Heart of Downtown
cards.subtitle: Maine Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk north from campus to find local favorites like Gelato Fiasco and Gulf of Maine Books in this vibrant commercial district.
cards.short_summary: Maine Street is the primary commercial corridor of Brunswick, connecting the Bowdoin campus to the town's historic downtown shops and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Street and the grassy Town Mall are favorite places to shop, dine and enjoy the vibrant community.
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7; business hours vary.

cards.title: Historic Federal District
cards.subtitle: Federal Street Historic District
cards.notes: View high-style Federal and Greek Revival architecture along this historic residential street bordering the north side of campus.
cards.short_summary: The Federal Street Historic District features 18th and 19th-century architecture and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.evidence_claim: The district includes a series of relatively high-style Federal and later-period houses along Federal Street and Maine Street.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; please respect private property.

cards.title: The Western Border
cards.subtitle: Park Row Corridor
cards.notes: Stroll past the Bowdoin College Museum of Art and the modern Park Row Apartments on this scenic campus-edge street.
cards.short_summary: Park Row runs along the western edge of the Bowdoin quad, housing major academic buildings and newer student apartments.
cards.evidence_claim: On the west side of the Quad along Park Row, the Mary Frances Searles Science Building (1894) houses the physics, mathematics, and computer science departments.
cards.access_notes: Public street with campus facilities; museum hours vary.

cards.title: The Route to Fat Boy
cards.subtitle: Bath Road Corridor
cards.notes: Head east on Bath Road to visit the iconic Fat Boy Drive-In, a seasonal Brunswick staple since the 1950s.
cards.short_summary: Bath Road serves as a major thoroughfare east of campus, leading to local landmarks and regional shopping.
cards.evidence_claim: Fat Boy | 111 Bath Road, Brunswick... The '50s style drive-in is a seasonal affair, with its fast food available from mid-March to mid-October.
cards.source_title: A visitor's guide to Brunswick, Maine - The Bowdoin Orient
cards.access_notes: Public road; Fat Boy is seasonal (March-October).

cards.title: The Gateway to Town
cards.subtitle: Pleasant Street Corridor
cards.notes: This busy corridor connects I-295 to downtown and features various local services and the historic Citizen building.
cards.short_summary: Pleasant Street is a primary entry point into Brunswick, hosting a mix of commercial businesses and residential conversions.
cards.evidence_claim: From I-295, take Route 1 North/Pleasant Street. Proceed to the third traffic light.

cards.title: The Transit Hub
cards.subtitle: Station Avenue District
cards.notes: Catch the Amtrak Downeaster or visit the Brunswick Visitor Center located just off Maine Street on this transit-focused block.
cards.short_summary: Station Avenue is the hub for regional rail and bus travel, located steps from the Bowdoin campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brunswick Hotel is a 51-room boutique hotel conveniently located at the top of Maine Street, nestled between Bowdoin College and The Downeaster Train Station.
cards.access_notes: Public transit area; train schedules vary.

cards.title: The Riverfront District
cards.subtitle: Mill Street / Fort Andross
cards.notes: Explore the massive Fort Andross mill complex for antiques, art studios, and views of the Androscoggin River.
cards.short_summary: Mill Street leads to the historic Fort Andross complex, a repurposed textile mill that now serves as a business and arts hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Cabot Mill Antiques – is a multi-dealer antique emporium located in Fort Andross, a beautifully restored textile mill on the Androscoggin River.
cards.access_notes: Public street; mill complex open during business hours.

cards.title: Downtown Living
cards.subtitle: Union Street Corridor
cards.notes: A key residential street for off-campus students, featuring historic multi-unit apartments close to downtown amenities.
cards.short_summary: Union Street provides a mix of residential housing options for the Brunswick community and upperclassmen living off-campus.
cards.evidence_claim: 84 Union St in Brunswick is ready for you to move in. This community can be found in Brunswick on Union St.

cards.title: The Community Square
cards.subtitle: Town Hall Place District
cards.notes: Located near the Town Mall, this area hosts community gatherings and is home to local eateries like Enoteca Athena.
cards.short_summary: Town Hall Place is a small connector near the Brunswick Town Mall, serving as a focal point for local dining and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Enoteca Athena... Brunswick's Italian and Greek wine bar and restaurant... located near the top of Maine Street.
cards.access_notes: Public area near the Town Mall.

cards.title: The Local Connector
cards.subtitle: Cushing Street Corridor
cards.notes: A quiet street featuring a mix of small retail spaces and residential units, just a short walk from the Maine Street action.
cards.short_summary: Cushing Street offers a quieter alternative to Maine Street with local retail and residential character.
cards.evidence_claim: 15 Cushing Street Brunswick, ME 04011 is a commercial property for lease... The property type is Retail Space.
